findings.title: Bound SDK-generated invalid-input errors before they bypass the result packager
findings.trigger: Call academy_teacher_report with a valid student selector plus an unrecognized property whose name is 'invented_' followed by 550000 ASCII 'k' characters. This is below the installed SDK stdio input buffer limit.
findings.reproduction: Use the production createTeacherServer, actual SDK Client and linked InMemoryTransport. Round-trip every server message through the installed serializeMessage/deserializeMessage functions. Submit the malformed arguments via client.callTool.
findings.expected: Invalid-input refusals must remain bounded and must not echo arbitrarily long caller field names. The source callback should remain uncalled.
findings.cause: Automatic SDK inputSchema validation runs before the registered handler and its toolResult/service budget logic. The strict-object error includes the untrusted unknown key, so the normal bounded consumer refusal path is never entered.
findings.effect: An advertised 512 KiB result boundary is exceeded on a real SDK error path even though successful query/report pages are packed correctly.
findings.repair: Use an SDK-supported bounded validation/error mapping or an owner-local bounded request/error boundary before automatic schema-error serialization. Preserve strict schemas and existing canonical consumption; do not fork SDK/common implementation or raise the result cap.
findings.requiredVerification: Exercise both tools via the actual SDK with long unknown keys, nested malformed selectors and multiple unknown fields; measure the complete error CallToolResult and confirm a fixed bounded refusal without input echo.

findings.title: Render catalog parent links instead of treating every catalog entry as a single hierarchy
findings.trigger: Render the unchanged canonical retainedFixture assignment, whose problem-1 and problem-2 nodes both have parent page.
findings.reproduction: Load teacherFixture(0), reconstruct its student scene with binding.readDocument, and pass that exact canonical document to renderTeacherReport. Inspect the work-A catalog parent fields and corresponding report line.

observed.reportChain: Invented major > Invented middle > Invented minor > Invented section > Invented page > Invented problem-1 > Invented problem-2

findings.expected: Sibling problems and separate branches must remain siblings/branches. Display only source-backed parent-child chains and preserve exact labels and edition-local scope.
findings.cause: All non-book catalog nodes, including sibling problems or sections, are flattened and joined with ' > ' without consulting node.parent.
findings.effect: The teacher-facing report invents a containment relation and can imply that one sibling item/unit contains another, despite correct canonical data.
findings.repair: Use the existing catalog IDs and parent links for presentation. Render each selected section/item under its own qualified ancestor path, group siblings explicitly, and leave missing parent levels unknown. Do not infer a new hierarchy or domain relationship.
findings.requiredVerification: Use multiple sibling problems, sibling sections and separate branches in one exact assignment; assert the report never serializes siblings as a parent-child chain.

findings.title: Do not print a blanket physical-stage unknown when the canonical review confirms printing
findings.trigger: The canonical assignment has an exact attempt-bound teacher review with paperStages.printed known/done and distributed unknown, tied to the same retained issuance.
findings.reproduction: Add an invented schema-valid teacher_activity_review through the synthetic TeacherReadStore studentWorkspaces seam, retain the exact assignment/attempt/issuance binding, and reconstruct through the canonical TeacherApplication and reader before rendering.
findings.expected: Print and distribution remain independent. Known printing must stay known while distribution remains unknown; a generic issuance caveat must not contradict an existing scoped observation.
findings.cause: Every assignment unconditionally receives the statement that actual printing and distribution are unknown. Later JSON summaries preserve the known observation, leaving contradictory statements in the same report.
findings.effect: A teacher relying on the plain report can treat an already observed print stage as unknown, despite qualified canonical evidence.
findings.repair: Replace the unconditional stage claim with a statement limited to what issuance alone proves, or present the existing canonical review's scoped stages explicitly. Preserve differing attempts/issuances and do not infer printing or distribution from scores.
findings.requiredVerification: Check printed-known/distributed-unknown, printed-unknown/distributed-known, both-unknown and mismatched issuance cases through the real canonical projection and report path.

findings.title: Preserve the teacher's reported clock separately from storage clocks
findings.trigger: A canonical teacher review carries payload.reportedAt that differs from its record.recordedAt.
findings.reproduction: In the same exact-bound synthetic review as C07, set payload.reportedAt to 2090-01-01T12:00:00.000Z and record.recordedAt to 2090-01-02T00:00:00.000Z. Validate the teacher payload, reconstruct the canonical scene and render the report.
findings.expected: Retain the available teacher-reported time and label it separately from source observation, verification, storage and query retrieval clocks. Do not silently discard the clock needed to place a scoped judgment in its dated history.
findings.cause: The generic clocks/evidence helpers read only sourceObservedAt, lastVerifiedAt and recordedAt. The review lines print a derived summary but not the underlying payload.reportedAt.
findings.effect: The report loses available dated teacher provenance while showing a different storage clock; readers cannot determine the teacher-report timing from the report itself.
findings.repair: Include the canonical teacher payload's reportedAt in the scoped review evidence presentation, with an explicit separate label. Keep unavailable clocks unknown and avoid substituting recordedAt or retrieval time.
findings.requiredVerification: Use differing teacher-reported, recorded and retrieved times, including a business-date boundary, and assert all available clocks remain distinct and attributable.
